To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
informal payments for public health care are highly regressive; the burden is highest for hospital care; the burden is lower for GP care; and, the burden is higher for outpatient specialist care.

(1) informal payments are a regressive way of financing health care, (2) the burden of informal payment falls more heavily on the poor, and (3) informal payments have a strong impact on the financial situation of poor households.
informal payments for health services are widespread, regressive and a significant burden on the poor.

the equity effects of informal payments for public health care in Hungary.

the Hungarian health care financing system is not equitable and that it needs urgent reform.
